topic: What moves a 30 year plan is what repeats, not what feels expensive

assumptions.notes: All figures are what the money would have become if invested instead at 6% real annual growth for 30 years. A one time €4,000 becomes €22,974 (4,000 x 1.06^30), shown as €23,000. €150 a month becomes €146,177 (monthly contributions, annual effective rate), shown as €146,000. The ratio is 6.4, shown as 6x. The quick test uses the same middle rate multipliers as the day 1 reel: a one time amount times 6 (exact 5.74) and a monthly amount times 1,000 (exact 974.5). €80 a month is €77,961, shown as about €80,000. All figures illustrative.

hookVariants.narration: A four thousand euro holiday, or a hundred and fifty euros more rent. Which one costs you more?
The purchase you feel worst about is rarely the one that costs you most.

beats.narration: Eva took a four thousand euro holiday. Invested instead for thirty years, that would be about twenty three thousand.
The same year she moved to a nicer flat. A hundred and fifty euros more rent, every month.
Invested instead, that is about a hundred and forty six thousand. Six times the holiday.
Guilt follows how loud a purchase is. The arithmetic follows how often it repeats.
A quick test. For a one time cost, multiply by six. For a monthly cost, multiply by a thousand.

You feel guilty about the four thousand euro holiday. A hundred and fifty more a month adds up to six times as much.

A one time €4,000, invested instead for 30 years, would be about €23,000. €150 a month more rent would be about €146,000. Six times as much, and nobody feels guilty about rent.

Guilt follows how loud a purchase is. The arithmetic follows how often it repeats.
